# `{upxdvir}`

The `{upxdvir}` package enables vertically typeset results to be converted to \textsf{R} objects and used with `{ggplot}` visualisations.

## Setup

`{upxdvir}` typesetting pipeline uses the up\LaTeX{} typesetting engine. The following system requirements are required to be installed prior to usage.

A TeX Live installation is required, steps to install a distribution can be found here: https://www.tug.org/texlive/. A minimal installation such as `tinytex` may also be used.

### *nix

The following dependencies should be installed with a package manager, such as `apt`.
Required packages: latexmk, texlive-lang-japanese, libuv1-dev, libfontconfig1-dev, libfreetype-dev, libharfbuzz-dev, libfribidi-dev, libfreetype6-dev, libpng-dev, libtiff5-dev, libjpeg-dev, libwebp-dev, texlive-latex-base

### macOS, Windows: 

The following can be installed using the `tlmgr` binary which is bundled with TeX installations.

Required packages: ipaex, japanese-otf, latexmk, lm, ptex, ptex-base, ptex-fontmaps, uplatex, uptex, uptex-base, uptex-fonts, pxrubrica, plext

```{r, echo = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE,
    comment = "#>",
    dev = "ragg_png",
    dpi = 120
)
options(upxdvir.pfb = TRUE)
drawGrid <- function(border = TRUE) {
    grid.segments(
        c(0, .5),
        c(.5, 0),
        c(1, .5),
        c(.5, 1),
        gp = gpar(lty = 4, col = "gray", alpha = .5)
    )
    if (border) {
        grid.rect(gp = gpar(lwd = 10, col = 2, fill = NA))
    }
}

setKnitrPresets <- function(
  height = 3, width = 3, error = TRUE, align = "center"
) {
    chunkSet <- knitr::opts_chunk$set
    chunkSet(error = error)
    chunkSet(fig.height = height)
    chunkSet(fig.width = width)
    chunkSet(fig.align = align)
}

setKnitrPresets(4, 4)
```

```{r setup}
library(grid)
library(upxdvir)
```

## Example Usage

`{upxdvir}` is a vertical typesetting extension to `{xdvir}`. There are two ways of interacting with this API:

1. Using the `{xdvir}` API, with parameters set to values that allow vertical typesetting. For example:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
grid.latex(
    "Text",
    engine = "upLaTeX",
    documentClass = "utarticle",
    fontLib = HBfontLibrary
)
latexGrob("Text",
    engine = "upLaTeX",
    documentClass = "utarticle",
    fontLib = HBfontLibrary
)
element_latex(
    engine = "upLaTeX",
    documentClass = "utarticle",
    fontLib = HBfontLibrary
)
```

2. Using the `{upxdvir}` API, which is a thin, convenience layer on top of the `{xdvir}` API, and sets the parameters up assuming vertical typesetting.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
grid.uplatex("Text")
uplatexGrob("Text")
element_uplatex()
```

## Vertical Typesetting

This is the most basic way of typesetting vertically (which is the default typesetting direction). Typesetting direction may be changed by setting the parameter `direction = "horizontal"`.

```{r vert}
drawGrid()
grid.uplatex(
    "The text is rendered vertically by default.",
    y = .8,
    direction = "horizontal"
)
grid.uplatex("「JRまで 0.5 km」と聞いた。")
```

## `{ggplot2}` Example

In more practical context, vertical typesetting is used with `{ggplot2}` visualisations. In the following examples, two different ways of vertical typesetting with `{ggplot2}` are shown.

1. `element_uplatex` - Used to `theme` non-data elements of a `{ggplot2}` visualisation, such as axis titles, labels and other annotations. The x and y axes, the main plot title are typeset using this interface.
1. `uplatexGrob` - Used to place text labels as annotations in the plot region. The annotations toward the top right of the plot are typeset using this interface.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
setKnitrPresets(5, 5)
```
```{r ggp, message = FALSE}
library(gggrid)

label <- function(data, coords) {
    uplatexGrob(
        "このグラフは、自動車の燃費とエンジン排気量との関係を示しています。",
        x = coords$x, y = coords$y,
        hjust = 1, vjust = 1, height = unit(1, "in")
    )
}

gg <- ggplot(mtcars) +
    geom_point(aes(x = disp, y = mpg))

gg +
    labs(
        x = "エンジン排気量 (Engine Displacement)",
        y = "燃費 (Miles per gallon)",
        title = "エンジン排気量と燃費の関係",
        subtitle = "Engine Displacement vs Fuel Economy"
    ) +
    theme(
        axis.title.x = element_uplatex(direction = "horizontal"),
        axis.title.y = element_uplatex(),
        plot.title = element_uplatex(
            direction = "horizontal", family = "serif", fontface = "bold"
        )
    ) +
    grid_panel(
        label,
        data = data.frame(x = max(mtcars$disp), y = max(mtcars$mpg)),
        aes(x, y)
    )
```

### Wrapped Text

When typesetting horizontally, multi-line paragraphs wrap using the width of the device and lines progress from top to bottom.
When typesetting vertically, wrapping is driven by the height instead, and lines progress from left to right. An example is shown in the following plot.

```{r height-ex}
grid.uplatex(
    "確率変数 $Z$ は、平均0、分散1の標準正規分布 $Z \\sim \\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ に従います。",
    gp = grid::gpar(height = grid::unit(2, "inches"))
)
```

Height can be specified either as explict `grid::unit` objects, or a plain numeric value, interpreted between 0 - 1 as the `{grid}` NPC value.

## Horizontal Typesetting

This example outlines a simple example where Japanese text is typeset using the left-to-right horizontal typesetting.

```{r, echo = FALSE}
setKnitrPresets(4, 4)
```

```{r horiz}
drawGrid()
grid.uplatex(
    paste(
        "The \\texttt{direction = \"horizontal\"}",
        "parameter typesets text horizontally."
    ),
    gp = gpar(width = unit(3, "in")),
    y = .75, direction = "horizontal"
)
grid.uplatex("「JRまで 0.5 km」と聞いた。", direction = "horizontal")
```

## Mathematical Symbols and Operators

Mathematical symbols and operators can be enclosed within `$ $` or `\[\]` and used with CJK text typeset vertically.

```{r e1}
mathText <- c(
    "二次式 $ax^2 + bx + c$ を考えます。",
    "分数 $\\frac{a}{b}$ を計算します（ただし、$b \\neq 0$ とします）。",
    "確率変数 $Z$ は、平均0、分散1の標準正規分布 $Z \\sim \\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$ に従います。"
)
drawGrid()
grid.uplatex(mathText, x = c(0.3, 0.5, 0.7), gp = gpar(height = .5))
```

## Annotations

Annotations (_Furigana_) are used in Japanese text to provide more context, translation, or pronunciation hints to the main text. In the following example, the annotation "Japanese Language" which is a translation for the main text "日本語" is typeset to the right of the main text. In horizontal typesetting, these would be place above the main text.

```{r annotations}
drawGrid()
grid.uplatex(
    "\\aruby{日本語}{Japanese language}を勉強しています。",
    y = .95, vjust = 1, gp = gpar(fontsize = 16)
)

grid.uplatex(
    "\\aruby{日本語}{Japanese language}を勉強しています。",
    y = .2, dir = "h", gp = gpar(fontsize = 16)
)
```

## Font Customisation

Font customisation is supported from presets offered by the `{pxchfon}` package,  such as the following:

1. `ipa`
1. `ipaex`
1. `haranoaji`
1. `sourcehan`
1. `noto`

A comprehensive list of font families that can be supported, subject to font installation, can be obtained by `upxdvir:::.getPtexFonts()`.

Only `plain` and `bold` font faces are supported since Japanese glyphs are already monospaced.

Examples for both font family and face customisation are presented in the following section.

### Font Families

```{r, echo = FALSE}
setKnitrPresets(5, 5)
```

```{r families}
drawGrid()
fontfamilies <- c("sourcehan", "serif", "noto", "ipaex", "haranoaji")
xs <- seq(.1, .9, by = .2)
invisible(mapply(
    \(x, fam, fac) {
        grid.latex(fam, x = x, y = .75)
        grid.uplatex(
            "これはフォントです。",
            x = x,
            gp = gpar(fontfamily = fam)
        )
    },
    xs, fontfamilies
))
```

### Font Faces

```{r faces}
drawGrid()
invisible(mapply(
    \(x, fam, fac) {
        grid.latex(fam, x = x, y = .75)
        grid.uplatex(
            "これはフォントです。",
            x = x,
            gp = gpar(fontfamily = fam, fontface = "bold")
        )
    },
    xs, fontfamilies
))
```
